newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha steady, arbitrage East helps sellers.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha steady, arbitrage East helps sellers.

text.p: European spot naphtha prices were steady to slightly firmer on Tuesday in thin trade.
Traders said buyers and sellers remained at a stand-off but sellers were beginning to gain the upper hand over relaxed European buyers with further arbitrage options East seen.
Forward paper markets were slightly firmer with the narrow backwardation to May swaps wiped out reflecting perceptions of further demand from the Far East.

This demand is seen in order to cover a supply deficit in the Asia-Pacific region that is likely to grow this year as a series of new petrochemical plants mainly in Singapore, Thailand, Indonesia and India create new demand.
Open spec and Russian cargoes on offer in NWE at around $195 a tonne were attracting little buying interest, but material in the Far East is still valued around $229 for May 16-31 delivery.
